research_rationale: EO 12261 of January 5, 1981, Gasohol in Federal Motor Vehicles (46 FR 2023, FR Doc. 81-832; published January 8, 1981), was read in full from the held Federal Register text. Issued under section 271 of the Energy Security Act (42 U.S.C. 8871), it requires Federal agencies to specify gasohol as an acceptable substitute in unleaded-gasoline procurements with a preference for gasohol (1-101), allows blending (1-102), sets feasibility and vehicle-designation factors (1-103, 1-104), ties Department of Defense use to section 815 of the Department of Defense Authorization Act, 1980 (1-105), excepts experimental fuel vehicles (1-106), delegates the President's section 271(b) exception authority (1-107), requires agencies to report gasohol usage data to the Department of Energy (1-108), defines gasohol (1-109) and requires implementing guidelines (1-110). The order has no end date. No held instrument amends, revokes or supersedes it: the only held texts that cite its number are its own printing and the 1989 OFR codification; the bounded searches located no later instrument; and the current-law:usc search found the order printed under 42 U.S.C. 8871 and 10 U.S.C. 2922c(a) referring to it by number. All eleven clauses are operative on 2026-10-14. The inventory is unchanged from the dossier (the preamble recites authority and purpose and is not a separate command).
savings_reason: The order has no savings clause and was not revoked or superseded, so no savings question arises; the bounded searches found no later instrument that preserves, revives or transfers a part of it.
earlier_end_check: Searched the held corpus for the number 'Executive Order 12261' (cruden): only its own Federal Register printing and the 1989 OFR codification text cite it, and the 1989 text is an editorial print. The bounded machine searches returned 2 U.S. Code hits (the print of the order under 42 U.S.C. 8871 and the reference in 10 U.S.C. 2922c), 0 eCFR hits and 0 OFR catalog hits. No own-terms end exists (no date, condition or sunset), and the order's authority recital cites section 271 of the Energy Security Act; no held instrument is shown to have ended that authority. Nothing earlier than 2026-10-14 ends any clause.
scope_check: Each numbered paragraph was read as its own clause. 1-101 to 1-104 bind Federal agencies as procurers and vehicle owners; 1-105 addresses only Department of Defense use under section 815 of the 1980 Defense Authorization Act; 1-106 is an exception; 1-107 delegates section 271(b) to the Secretary of Defense (DoD use) and the Administrator of General Services (other agencies); 1-108 binds agencies to supply data on request; 1-109 is a definition; 1-110 directs guidelines. No instrument is held that amends or limits any of them, and the Department of Energy, Secretary of Defense and Administrator of General Services remain the addressees.
independent_command_check: The standing commands (procurement preference and blending allowance, feasibility factors, vehicle designation, the DoD use rule, the exception, the delegation, the data-sharing duty, the definition and the guideline duty) each operate continuously. 1-110's guideline duty is not a one-time command with a deadline: no deadline is stated and no held source shows guidelines issued or withdrawn, so it is recorded operative rather than performed.
savings_check: No savings provision exists and none is needed; the order's commands operate prospectively and no accrued right or transferred function is at issue on the held record.

research_rationale: EO 12423 of May 26, 1983, Foreign Assistance and Arms Control (48 FR 24025, FR Doc. 83-14689), was read in full from the held Federal Register text. It has two operative sections, both amendments of other orders: section 1 adds section 636(i) to the functions listed in section 1-301(b) of EO 12163; section 2 restates section 1(d) of EO 11958 as a delegation to the Secretary of Defense of the functions under sections 22(a), 29 and 30 of the Act. Under the owner's strike-and-insert ruling (2026-10-21) an amendment clause continues, as amended, until the parent order ends. EO 12163 remains in force and no held later instrument rewrites subsection 1-301(b), so section 1 is operative on 2026-10-14. EO 11958 was revoked as amended by section 4 of EO 13637 of March 8, 2013, with its substance re-delegated in section 1(d) of EO 13637, so section 2 ended on 2013-03-08. EO 12560 section 11 (May 24, 1986) earlier restated section 1(d) to add the functions under section 30A; that amends the clause without ending it, and a human reviewer should note that the substance changed. The whole order is YES because section 1 is operative. The dossier chain lists many other amenders of EO 12163 and EO 11958; they are not later events of EO 12423 unless they change 1-301(b) or 1(d), and EO 13637 does not name EO 12163.
savings_reason: Section 2's delegation to the Secretary of Defense of the functions under sections 22(a), 29, 30 and 30A of the Arms Export Control Act was carried forward when EO 11958 was revoked: section 1(d) of EO 13637 delegates those functions to the Secretary of Defense, and section 4 of EO 13637 continues actions taken under EO 11958 to the extent consistent with it. The delegation survives under EO 13637, not under EO 12423 section 2.
earlier_end_check: Searched the held fr-originals texts of every instrument the dossier lists as amending EO 12163 or EO 11958 (EO 12458, 12500, 12560, 12608, 12620, 12639, 12680, 12695, 12738, 13030, 13091, 13118, 13284, 13346, 13361, 13637, 13656) for section 1-301 of EO 12163, the numbers 635(g) and 636(i), and section 1(d) of EO 11958. For section 1 none revokes or rewrites subsection (b). For section 2 only EO 12560 section 11 rewrites 1(d) before EO 13637 revokes EO 11958 on 2013-03-08. No own-terms end exists in EO 12423. No earlier end is shown for either clause.
scope_check: Section 1 reaches only subsection 1-301(b) of EO 12163; section 2 reaches only section 1(d) of EO 11958. EO 13637 revokes EO 11958 and its held text does not name EO 12163, so it ends section 2 but not section 1, even though the dossier's machine lead links it to both clauses through EO 11958 as amended.
independent_command_check: The two sections are independent amendments of separate parent orders. Section 1 continues while EO 12163 stands; section 2 ended on revocation of its parent. EO 12560 section 11 and EO 13637 section 1(d) are separate instruments with their own dates, not performance of section 2.
savings_check: EO 13637 section 4 revokes EO 11958 as amended but keeps actions taken under it in force to the extent consistent with EO 13637; EO 13637 section 1(d) re-delegates the functions section 2 had delegated. That is a transferred delegation, so savings is transferred_or_accrued.

research_rationale: EO 12908 of April 22, 1994, Order of Succession of Officers To Act as Secretary of the Army (59 FR 21907, FR Doc. 94-10241), was read in full from the held Federal Register text. Section 1 designates, in order, the Under Secretary of the Army, the Assistant Secretaries and General Counsel of the Army, and the Chief of Staff of the Army to act for the Secretary of the Army on death, permanent disability or resignation (paragraph (a)) or on absence or temporary disability (paragraph (b)), with precedence and acting-officer limits in paragraphs (c) and (d); section 2 states that succession is temporary or interim and does not vacate the successor's statutory appointment. The order is a standing designation with no end date. No held instrument amends, revokes or supersedes it: the bounded searches located none, and the only held text that cites its number is its own Federal Register and APP printing. The dossier's clause inventory omitted section 2 (the dossier span stopped inside the page break within paragraph (d)); the inventory is corrected to ten clauses covering sections 1 and 2, with the heading line of section 1 merged into paragraph (a). All ten clauses are operative on 2026-10-14.
savings_reason: The order states no savings or transitional clause and was not revoked, so there is no savings question: the standing designations in sections 1 and 2 themselves remain operative, and the bounded searches found no later instrument that preserves or revives a part of the order.
earlier_end_check: Searched the held corpus for the order's number and for orders of succession of the Secretary of the Army (cruden search). Only the order's own printings cite 12908. Earlier succession instruments (EO 10495, 10820, 12514 Part II) predate it and are not later events; none of them is held as naming EO 12908. The machine searches current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog returned 0 hits and current-law:usc returned 4 hits that are U.S. Code notes citing the order as the Army succession order, not amendments. No own-terms end exists. Nothing earlier than 2026-10-14 ends any clause.
scope_check: Each paragraph was read as its own clause. Paragraph (a) governs death, permanent disability or resignation; paragraph (b) governs absence or temporary disability and has two sub-paragraphs (acting designation lasts only for the absence; the Secretary may continue to exercise powers while temporarily absent); paragraph (c) assigns precedence among officers with the same date of appointment to the Secretary of the Army; paragraph (d) excludes officers serving only in an acting capacity; section 2 makes the succession temporary. The order's reach is the Department of the Army only and no instrument is held that amends the lists.
independent_command_check: The independent commands are the three-position succession lists (a)(1)-(a)(3), the temporary-absence rule (b) and its two sub-paragraphs, the precedence rule (c), the acting-capacity exclusion (d) and the temporary-nature rule in section 2. Each operates whenever a vacancy or absence occurs and none is a one-time command that has been performed, so none is exhausted before the cutoff.
savings_check: The order has no savings clause. Because it is a standing designation, no accrued or transferred right is at issue; the savings state records that the bounded searches found no residual instrument.
